newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT -Mehrtens sets sights on beating Auckland.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT -Mehrtens sets sights on beating Auckland.

text.p: TAURANGA, Aug 5 - All Black first five-eighth Andrew Mehrtens made 25 new mates last night -- now all he has to do is remember their names.
Mehrtens made a flying visit to the Bay of Plenty Steamers' training at Mount Maunganui's Blake Park, slotting into the side as they prepared for Wednesday's clash with Auckland, NZPA reports.
But while the 24-year-old took all of five minutes to pick up the Bay backline's calls, learning his new team-mates' names could take a little longer.
"I was made to feel pretty welcome out there by the guys, although I must admit a couple of times I wasn't sure if I was meeting a couple of the guys for the second time in the night," Mehrtens said.
"I knew I wouldn't pick up everyone's name in one night but I hope no one took it personally if I kept calling them mate'."
Mehrtens was offered the "guest spot" in the Steamers after the Bay union contacted All Black coach John Hart.
Mehrtens jumped at the chance to stretch his legs after a month on the sideline.
"This was the first time I had trained full-on for 10 or 11 days and it went really well and was quite enjoyable -- as much as anyone can ever enjoy training."
Mehrtens said he was "jumping out of his skin" to play the Aucklanders tomorrow.

"I've never beaten them and the Bay guys have a lot to prove after last year I guess. There's every incentive for the team to do well without me in the side -- I'm just here to fit into the team and do a job as well as I can without letting anyone down."

Mehrtens, who has relinquished his All Black spot to Carlos Spencer after suffering a leg injury, said he wouldn't even be thinking about his troublesome limb or his own international aspirations at the Tauranga Domain tomorrow.
He flew to Auckland to assemble with the All Black squad this morning but said he couldn't wait to get back for the midweek clash.
"My motivation isn't concentrated on the All Blacks. For me, my whole focus this week is on Wednesday and trying to get a win over Auckland and until that's over, nothing else matters.
